faq.q: How many chromosomes do we get from each parent?
faq.a: You get 23 chromosomes from your mother and 23 from your father, making 23 pairs and 46 in total in most of your cells.
asks: Where do our chromosomes come from?
How many chromosomes do humans have?

faq.q: Why do I have two versions of each gene?
faq.a: Because your chromosomes come in pairs, one from each parent, you have two copies of most genes. The copies can be slightly different versions, called alleles.
asks: Why do genes come in pairs?

faq.q: Why don't brothers and sisters look the same?
faq.a: Each parent passes on a random half of their chromosomes, and they are reshuffled every time an egg or sperm is made. So each child gets a different mix, unless they are identical twins.
asks: Why do I not look like my brother?

faq.q: Is everything about how I look decided by genes?
faq.a: No. Genes set a lot, but your environment matters too: food, sunlight, exercise, illness and life experiences all shape your body. Most features come from many genes plus the environment.

faq.q: Why do some children look more like one parent?
faq.a: Some versions of genes have stronger effects than others, and features like face shape depend on many genes at once. By chance, a child may get more of the versions that make them resemble one parent.
asks: Why do I look more like my dad?
Can you look like only one parent?

facts: Human body cells contain 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs.
Each parent can make over 8 million different combinations of chromosomes in their eggs or sperm, even before genes are shuffled within chromosomes.

quiz.say: How many chromosomes did you get from your father?
quiz.why: Each parent passes on 23 chromosomes, which together make your 23 pairs.

wrong.0: 46 is the total from both parents together.
wrong.2: You get one of each of 23 pairs from each parent, not just two.
